$doc: THE WIRE VOCABULARY — one manifest, four languages (#255).
Every name below used to live in two, three or four hand-maintained copies:
C# (NativeRenderer / FrameEncoder), Kotlin (YogaLayout, NativeFrameAdapter),
Objective-C++ (BnYogaLayout.mm) and Swift (BnFrameAdapter, and a test-side
list). A drift test parsed the literals back out of those files and asserted
they agreed — which caught divergence, but only AFTER it was written, and only
for the pairs somebody remembered to pin.
This file is now the source. tools/BlazorNative.WireGen emits every copy, and
WireVocabularyCodegenTests re-runs the emitters and byte-compares them against
the committed output, so a hand-edit of a generated file fails in the required
build-test lane. Divergence stops being REPRESENTABLE rather than merely
detected.
TO ADD A STYLE NAME: add it here, run `dotnet run --project
tools/BlazorNative.WireGen`, and commit the regenerated files. Then implement
it — a name accepted by the routing table that no shell applies is a style
SILENTLY DROPPED at runtime, which is the failure mode this whole apparatus
exists to prevent. AndroidSetStyleDispatch_HasAnArmForEveryYogaStyle is the pin
that makes that half fail loudly too.
Style names that are LAYOUT: the shells route these to the node's Yoga node,
never to the view. `padding`/`margin`/`width`/`height` are LAYOUT even though
they read as box properties — Yoga lays a container's children out inside its
padding box, so a shell that ALSO insets the view double-applies them.
NOT here, on purpose (no typed parameter and no producer, so accepting them
would be three hand-written parsers implementing a name nothing emits):
alignContent, rowGap, columnGap, display, flex. The wrap demo RELIES on Yoga's
alignContent default of flex-start — not setting it is precisely how it gets it.
Style names that are VISUAL: the shells route these to the View / UIView
(paint), never to Yoga. Disjoint from yogaStyles by construction, and pinned
disjoint by StyleAttributePartitionTests.
On a node of NodeType `scroll` these CONTAINER-layout names are IGNORED AND
LOGGED by both shells. A scroll node's only Yoga child is the synthetic content
node, so each of these fails silently and bafflingly: `gap` spaces one child
against nothing; `justifyContent` offsets the content to a NEGATIVE y (free
space on a scrolling viewport is negative) and permanently hides the top of the
page; `padding` moves every frame in the parity table.
Every name here MUST also be in yogaStyles — the rule is only reached once the
router has decided the name belongs to Yoga. A name here but not there would
never reach the rule: it would fall into the visual branch and be dropped.
The generator enforces that subset relation and refuses to emit otherwise.
Node types whose size is the native widget's business — and the ONLY nodes that
get a Yoga measure function. NOT 'the nodes with no children': a childless
`view` is a container, and measuring it would let its intrinsic size override
Yoga. `modal` is deliberately absent — it materializes as an anchor and an
overlay, both CONTAINERS, and a measure func on a container is a named
violation of the layout law.
CreateNode's widget class. `id` IS the wire value and is never renumbered or
reused: the shells index an array by it, so a shift would mean a shell
compiled against the old ids builds the wrong widget for every node.
id 0 is None — never emitted for a CreateNode. The shells still carry a slot
for it, holding the `?` fallback their index guard returns for any id past the
end of their array, which is exactly what a shell that missed a vocabulary
extension does until it catches up.
`enum` mirrors BlazorNative.Runtime.BlazorNativeNodeType. That enum is public
API with a PublicAPI baseline, so it is NOT generated — it is PINNED against
this list by WireVocabularyCodegenTests, which calls FrameEncoder.MapNodeType
for every wire name here and asserts the ordinal matches.
